title: The Halloween ghost train taking families to one of UK's most haunted castles
excerpt: Families can board a Halloween-themed train from Manchester for a spooky day out at one of the UK’s most haunted castles
content:
A ghostly train ride is promising a day of spooky family fun this Halloween.

The Muncaster Express will depart from Manchester Victoria on October 26, stopping at Preston, Lancaster, Carnforth and Ulverston on its way to the Western Lake District.

Passengers will disembark at Ravenglass before being taken by coach to the Muncaster Castle Halloween Family Festival.

Ewan Frost-Pennington, general manager at Muncaster, said: "I am thrilled that The Muncaster Express is returning this Halloween.

The Muncaster Express arriving at Ravenglass Station (Image: Supplied)

"It is one of our most popular annual experiences and is a unique way to get into the spooky spirit.

"We are very excited to be opening the Muncaster Halloween fun up to an even wider audience."

The Muncaster Express will also run from Carlisle on Wednesday, stopping at Penrith, Oxenholme, Carnforth and Ulverston.

Passengers will travel in vintage, diesel-hauled carriages decorated for Halloween, with on-board entertainment and scenic views of the Lake District.

Muncaster Castle is considered one of the UK’s most haunted castles.

Entertainment on board the Muncaster Express (Image: Supplied)

This year’s festival features a 'zombie-boggle apocalypse,' blending Cumbrian folklore with Halloween.

Visitors can explore the castle’s haunted rooms, enjoy bird of prey displays, and try their hand at archery, axe-throwing and crossbow in The Weapons Hall.

The festival also includes live entertainment in the gardens, Halloween trails, a scary maze, pumpkin carving, Halloween parades, costume competitions, and food.

Muncaster Castle (Image: Supplied)

Muncaster Express passengers will receive an exclusive 15 per cent discount on tickets to the new Castle Show, a promenade performance set inside the castle.

The show follows His Lordship Peter Frost-Pennington as he tries to rid the castle of troublesome boggles with help from two so-called experts, Ada Twanky and Madam Bridget.

Passengers wishing to claim the ticket discount should call 01229 717614 between 9am and 5pm.

The Muncaster Express is operated by West Coast Railways, with tickets starting at £49.50 for children and £59.50 for adults.

Tickets include return travel, on-board entertainment, coach transfers, entry to the festival, a pumpkin for each child, and access to the Castle Show discount.

All tickets must be booked in advance through the West Coast Railways website at westcoastrailways.co.uk/the-muncaster-express/details.
